content.text:
I built this as a small dependency-free ES module in `/tmp/discovery/run5/work/approvals/`, and all 6 tests pass with `npm test`.

**Library search:** I searched npm for truth-maintenance, JTMS, belief-revision and reason-maintenance packages. Nothing suitable came up; the hits were unrelated or agent-memory products. So I wrote a minimal version of the standard justification-based approach.

**How it works** (`approvals.js`, class `ApprovalLedger`):
- `approve(id, ...justifications)` records which evidence an approval rests on. Each justification is a list of evidence ids, and passing several gives alternatives. The approval stays valid while at least one justification is fully intact.
- `withdraw(evidenceId)` removes that evidence and returns only the approvals that just lost all support. Approvals that didn't use it are untouched.
- `restore(evidenceId)` brings evidence back, which revives any approval whose justification is whole again.
- `isValid(id)` and `needsReconsideration()` report current status.

**Tests** (`approvals.test.js`) cover these cases:
- Withdrawing `A` affects only the approval that used `A`.
- Withdrawing shared evidence affects both approvals.
- Withdrawing unrelated evidence changes nothing.
- An alternative justification keeps an approval valid.
- Restoring evidence revives the approval, and `withdraw` reports only new losses.
- Approving on withdrawn evidence, or with no justification, throws.

The first test run had one failure, which was a wrong assertion in my own test. I corrected the assertion and the module itself didn't change.

An approval whose support is withdrawn is only flagged as needing reconsideration. Nothing re-approves or revokes it automatically.
